clue.text: Bill made police arrest Mark as accessory

parts.note: a bill is an account, abbreviated ACC

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the shuffled police letters hold the mark inside them
made in the sense of fashioned anew, so the letters of police are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An invoice shows that officers detained a man named Mark as an accomplice to the crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges POLICE to OPLICE, which 'arrest' wraps round M to give OMPLICE, after ACC. In law an accessory is a partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory in criminal law is a person who assists in a crime, i.e. a partner in wrongdoing.

parts.note: A, as in A1 or grade A, marks the top quality
board is food provided regularly, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: First-class dining is laid on for passengers on a liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aboard is to be on a vessel, train or plane as a passenger or crew member.

clue.text: Varied cares besetting a Roman emperor

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the shuffled letters go round the a
varied means altered, so the letters of cares are put in another order

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler is beset by all manner of worries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' turns CARES into CAESR, and 'besetting' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius and Augustus bore the title, which became the name for any Roman emperor.

clue.text: Conduct of secret service gives offence

parts.note: MI (Military Intelligence, as in MI5 and MI6) is Britain's secret service; 'of' makes it the possessive MI'S
demeanour is behaviour or conduct

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour by spies causes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conduct of secret service' is MI'S DEMEANOUR, the secret service's conduct, so 'of' sets MI'S first. 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A misdemeanour is a minor crime or wrongdoing, a lesser kind of offence.

definitions.meaning: rich in the sense of luxuriant and abundant, like thick green growth
a heavy drinker, in American slang

explanation.definitionFit: Lush vegetation is rich and luxuriant, and a lush is US slang for a drunkard.

indicators.note: ordered means put in order, so the letters of spacemen and to are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Astronauts were told to cancel out the effects of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'effects' as part of the definition and the verb fails; 'offset' alone is the definition, and 'effects' is a link word making the surface sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To compensate is to make up for or counterbalance something, as a gain offsets a loss.

indicators.note: headed here means topped, so the letter for hot sits at the front of the member

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Injury done by a hothead who lashes out with a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot-headed' looks like one adjective for a short-tempered person, but it splits: H heads ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is injury or hurt, much the same as damage done to someone.

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the word for a primate takes the assumption inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
a posit is a statement assumed to be true, an assumption

explanation.surface: A monkey concedes that a hypothesis is suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite remarks are relevant and well suited to the occasion, i.e. pertinent.

clue.text: Butcher offered service to Crusader fort

parts.note: Mass is a church service
Acre, in modern Israel, was a great Crusader stronghold

explanation.surface: A butcher held a church service at a crusading castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' is a verb, to slaughter wholesale. 'offered' and 'to' are links: ACRE is the port city of Acre in present-day Israel, taken by the Crusaders.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter many people brutally, as a butcher kills animals.

clue.text: Charming words are the key to the door

definitions.text: Charming words are the key to the door

parts.words: Charming words are the key to the door
parts.note: charming in the sense of casting a spell: the magic phrase spoken in the Ali Baba tale that makes the robbers' cave swing open

explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale of Ali Baba the magic password unlocks the thieves' cave door.

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the drink and the nothing are read right to left

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone has nothing to drink when coming home from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SUP and O, giving OPUS. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a creative work, especially a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Arriving in hot pants has drawbacks

indicators.note: in places the arriving word within the word for hot pants

parts.note: hot pants are very brief shorts
coming means arriving

explanation.surface: Turning up in skimpy shorts has its disadvantages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcomings are faults or failings, the weak points of something.

parts.note: a bibliophagist devours books; at a British university the rank just below a professorial chair is that of a senior lecturer with this title

explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a reader ranks just below a professor (a chair); a bookworm curled within reach of an armchair is the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bibliophagist is a voracious devourer of books, and the senior academic rank below professor has the same name.

clue.text: Feel sure he's taken attorney to chapel

parts.note: to bet, as in 'I bet', is to feel sure of something
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: Confident that a man has hired a lawyer to go to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' is a link. Bethesda is a common name for Welsh nonconformist chapels, after the healing pool in John's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Welsh nonconformist chapels are named after the biblical pool of healing in Jerusalem, so the name stands for such a place of worship.

clue.text: Behaving like a Hollander and paying one's way

definitions.meaning: turning native in the Netherlands, acting like someone from Holland
each person in a group paying for their own share of the bill

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means becoming like a Netherlander; idiomatically it means splitting a restaurant bill so each pays separately.

clue.text: Rotterdam's no place for a protester

indicators.note: place used as a verb, to set in position, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Activists are not welcome in the Dutch port of Rotterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' rearranges ROTTERDAMS plus NO; the 'S of Rotterdam's counts as a letter here. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrator is someone who joins a public march or rally to protest.

indicators.note: headed means given a head, the first letter of swollen going in front

parts.note: a tripper is a tourist on a day trip

explanation.surface: A conceited holidaymaker who talks endlessly about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swollen-headed' wants to mean conceited, but it gives S, the head of 'Swollen', placed before TRIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease performer reveals herself in a literal sense by taking off clothes.

parts.note: skip, short for skipper, is a ship's captain
Jack is a familiar form of the name John

explanation.surface: A fish dish intended for Captain John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack is a type of tuna that leaps from the water, a commercially fished species.

parts.note: taking means charming or appealing, as in her taking ways
a notice is a posted announcement or advertisement

explanation.surface: Seeing an eye-catching poster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be observing something is to pay attention to it, the idiom for heeding.

clue.text: The man had time to become a climber

parts.note: he refers to a man
the contracted form of had, as in he'd, is D
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A mountaineer spent a long time getting up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link. Hedera is the botanical name of ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the genus of ivy, a plant that clings and grows up walls and trees.

clue.text: Hardly the seat in which to sink down

definitions.meaning: a high-backed wooden bench, the seat being hard rather than cushioned
to subside or descend gradually, as sediment comes to rest

explanation.walkthrough: 'in which to' is a link. The joke: a wooden bench is hardly a seat to sink into.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an old wooden bench with a high back; the verb means to subside or come to rest.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a grand is a thousand pounds, M being the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' gives M POUNDS: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds, and M is the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound goods is to seize them by legal authority, i.e. take them into custody.

parts.note: the proud claim 'I am', its English half giving AM
pere is French for father

explanation.surface: A half-English, half-French dad brags about what he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anglo-French' says the boast mixes languages: English AM, French PÈRE, 'I am father'. The ampere is the unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit for measuring the strength of an electric flow.

clue.text: Joplin piece based on a Hindu composition

parts.note: Scott Joplin wrote piano rags such as The Entertainer

explanation.surface: A ragtime tune derived from Indian classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'based on' puts RAG on top of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music on which performers improvise.

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in musical notation
a lay is a narrative poem or ballad

explanation.surface: A soft song makes for a pleasant diversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama staged in a theatre, a form of amusement.

clue.text: What can be accomplished by people in disgrace?

definitions.text: What can be accomplished by people in disgrace?

parts.words: What can be accomplished by people in disgrace?
parts.note: the clue asks for something achieved; the word splits as AT TAIN MEN, near enough men under attainder, disgraced by having their rights forfeited

explanation.walkthrough: Attainder was the old legal disgrace of losing civil rights; the clue plays on 'attaint men' while asking simply for an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is an achievement or accomplishment.

definitions.meaning: a slope or tilt, as of a theatre stage

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A raked stage slopes towards the audience, and a dissolute man about town is called the same.

parts.note: cheap means inexpensive
a skate is a flat ray-like fish

explanation.surface: A miser buys bargain fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who hates spending money is a tightwad or penny-pincher.
